comments.text:
The single biggest trap on Dalal Street is convincing retail traders that buying cheap out-of-the-money options on expiry day is a 'low risk' lottery.

Official SEBI regulatory data tracking over 45 lakh Indian retail traders revealed that 93% lost money in F&O, with average cumulative losses of Rs. 1.25 Lakh per person. On expiry day, Theta decay accelerates exponentially; quantitative studies show that over 98% of out-of-the-money options melt to exactly Rs. 0.00 by 3:15 PM. Promoting low-margin expiry bets as an easy profit strategy treats derivatives like a lottery where the odds are overwhelmingly stacked against the buyer.

Before risking hard-earned capital on high-volatility expiry trades or unverified social media tips, review the audited regulatory statistics. Mathematical probability always beats speculative noise.

— PaisaFactCheck

Drawing textbook horizontal support and resistance lines looks simple in retrospect, but modern algorithmic market microstructure makes it a retail liquidity trap.

Static horizontal lines ignore institutional order-flow mechanics and algorithmic liquidity sweeps. In modern electronic markets dominated by high-frequency trading (HFT) and institutional algorithms, visible retail support and resistance levels are frequently target zones for liquidity sweeps—triggering retail stop-loss clusters before reversing. Relying on basic textbook chart patterns without understanding volume profile, delta, or Greeks leads to persistent false breakouts.

Stop treating textbook chart lines like crystal balls. Consistent trading edge comes from understanding institutional liquidity and position sizing, not visual pattern projection.

— PaisaFactCheck
